prompt: Read this NestJS CSRF middleware out loud with me: on safe requests it mints a random token into a `csrf-token` cookie, and on mutating requests (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) it's supposed to reject any request where the `x-csrf-token` header doesn't match that cookie. QA built a proof-of-concept auto-submitting cross-site form, and it still succeeded against a victim with a fresh session — no CSRF cookie had ever been minted for them — even though this middleware is wired in front of every mutating route and its unit tests are all green. Walk me through why the double-submit check lets that forged request through, and tell me how you'd fix it.
